## Two notes added after the results, and nothing above this line was touched

**The signature block was never filled in.** It is left blank rather than
backfilled: writing a date and a SHA now would assert a registration moment that
did not happen, which is worse than an unsigned pre-registration. What the
commit history does establish is that the predictions above were committed
before `eval/results/` contained any of the numbers they concern, and that is
the property the exercise depends on.

**The measured column stays empty on purpose.** `_(after)_` is not an oversight;
this file is frozen and the comparison lives in
[`eval/results/prereg_diff.md`](../eval/results/prereg_diff.md), which is
generated by `eval/report.py` and never hand-edited. **Most of the predictions
above went against us**, and the diff counts them rather than this sentence
asserting a number that would go stale the next time the ablation runs. The one
that has held throughout is the one the pitch rests on: ranking alerts by how
loud they are predicts catastrophe no better than a coin.

One of them — H4 — was written down *expecting* to lose, and it lost in the
direction we did not expect: the learned kernel beat static betweenness on
ranking by more than the margin we said it would not exceed. Being wrong in your
own favour is the case that deserves the most scrutiny, so the ablation rather
than the AUC table is where that claim should be judged.
